hook: A 5 mm motor shreds twelve 3D modules in under 30 seconds.

sections.voiceover: A 5 mm motor shreds twelve 3D modules in under 30 seconds.
sections.visual_cue: Close‑up of a 5 mm vibration motor beside a stack of 3D‑printed cuboctahedral modules.

sections.voiceover: On 23 January 2026, University of Washington scientists demonstrated a motor separating 3D modules. How could it detach up to twelve modules in under 30 seconds?
sections.visual_cue: Screenshot of the Nature Communications article dated 23 January 2026 with the University of Washington logo.

sections.voiceover: Yet the system contains no electronics, only the vibrating motor.
sections.visual_cue: Diagram highlighting the motor without any electronic components, showing only the vibrating element.

sections.voiceover: A 5 mm motor ripped twelve cuboctahedral modules apart in 30 seconds. The proof shows a coin‑sized device can safely dismantle complex assemblies.
sections.visual_cue: Time‑lapse of the motor detaching twelve modules in 30 seconds, followed by a graphic of scalable de‑construction.

sections.voiceover: Twelve modules fell apart in just 30 seconds.
sections.visual_cue: Final frame overlaying "12 modules" and "30 seconds" on the motor.
